## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Indriyabaddhakathā* (Kv 17.4) is a doctrinal controversy located in the seventeenth chapter (*vagga*) of the *Kathāvatthu*, the fifth treatise of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Catalog record]. The controversy centers on whether *dukkha* (suffering) is solely bound up with the sentient faculties (*indriyabaddha*) or can also be not bound up with the faculties (*anindriyabaddha*) [Dube 1980]. According to Buddhaghosa's commentary, *dukkha* is divided into that which is bound up with the faculties and that which is not bound up with them, whereby even insentient things may be termed *dukkha* because they serve as causal factors in suffering; by contrast, the Hetuvādins did not distinguish between these two modes [Dube 1980]. Modern scholarship notes that this debate pivots on whether *indriyabaddha dukkha* denotes strictly physical sensation or subjective experiential unhappiness as distinguished from external material conditions [Dube 1980].
